newsitem.title: HAITI: Rain from Tropical Storm Marco hits Hispaniola.
newsitem.headline: Rain from Tropical Storm Marco hits Hispaniola.

text.p: Tropical Storm Marco drifted aimlessly over the Caribbean on Friday and its rains spread to Haiti and the Dominican Republic on Hispaniola island, raising a threat of flash floods and mudslides.
Haiti and the Dominican Republic were already inundated with heavy rain from another storm system.

Haiti, where decades of deforestation and erosion have heightened the risk of flooding, had experienced showers from the outer fringes of Marco but expected worse in coming days. Radio Inter reported on Friday that 26 people had been killed during the past week as a result of flooding.
Marco "is moving very, very slowly. Haiti can expect a lot of rain from the southern coast up to the Grande Anse," said Renan Jean-Louis, a meteorologist with government television.

A state of emergency was in effect in the north and northeast regions of the Dominican Republic after four days of heavy rain from the other storm system, and the government warned that Marco could bring more flooding.

At 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT), the centre of Marco was at latitude 16.0 north, longitude 74.9 west, about 180 miles (295 km) southeast of Kingston, Jamaica. It was moving slowly to the northeast, but little motion was expected through Saturday, meteorologists at the U.S. National Hurricane Centre said.
"It looks right now like it will do some slow meandering, making Jamaica and Hispaniola nervous for the next couple of days," Mike Hopkins, hurricane centre meteorologist, said.
Marco weakened Friday afternoon, with maximum sustained winds dropping from 65 mph (100 kph) to 50 mph (80 kph), forecasters said. Heavy rain was occurring primarily over the Caribbean Sea.

The Dominican government on Friday dispatched aid workers to flooded areas and prepared to deliver food, medicine, mattresses and blankets to familes forced to abandon their houses because of flooding from swollen rivers and brooks.
